```{r}
library(tidyverse) # for data wrangling
library(reshape2)
library(matrixStats)
library(gridExtra)

#Importing Data

#metadata and filtered feature matrix 
studies = c("Zeevi_2014","Brito_2016","OhJ_2014_filtered")

meta_dfs_unfiltered = list()
meta_dfs = list()
count_dfs_unfiltered = list()
count_dfs = list()

#filtering parameters to filter count matrix

#All input data tables were
# filtered within SIMBA for prevalence (at least 5% across the complete dataset) and abun-
# dance (maximum relative abundance across samples of at least 1e-04

ab.cutoff = 1e-04 #eliminates features that have less than this relative abundance (presumably across all samples)
prev.cutoff = 0.05 #eliminates features with less than this prevalence
log.n0 = 1e-05

filt.params = list(ab.cutoff=as.numeric(ab.cutoff),
                   prev.cutoff=prev.cutoff,
                   log.n0=as.numeric(log.n0))

for(i in 1:length(studies)){

  #Importing and Filtering Data as in SimbaR simulation workflow
  meta_filename = paste0("raw_data/meta_",studies[i],".tsv")
  motu_filename = paste0("raw_data/motus_",studies[i],".tsv")
  
  meta = read_tsv(meta_filename, col_types = cols()) %>% 
    filter(!is.na(Sample_ID)) %>%
    as.data.frame()
  
  rownames(meta) <- meta$Sample_ID
  
  feat = read.table(motu_filename, sep='\t', stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                        check.names = FALSE, quote = '', comment.char = '',
                        row.names = 1, header = TRUE)
  
  meta_dfs_unfiltered[[studies[i]]] = meta
  count_dfs_unfiltered[[studies[i]]] = feat
  
  res <- simbaR:::check.original.data(feat, meta, sim.type="cross-section", sim.method="resampling")
  feat.checked <- res$feat
  meta.checked <- res$meta
  
  #Filtering
  filt.params <- simbaR:::check.filtering.parameters(filt.params)
  feat.filt <- simbaR:::filter.data(feat = feat.checked, meta = meta.checked, filt.params = filt.params)
  
  filtered_ids = meta.checked$Individual_ID
  
  meta.filtered = meta %>% filter(Individual_ID %in% filtered_ids)
  
  meta_dfs[[studies[i]]] = meta.filtered
  count_dfs[[studies[i]]] = feat.filt
  
}
```

```{r}
#Sparsity of each matrix
for(study in studies){
  sparsity = sum(count_dfs[[study]] == 0)/(dim(count_dfs[[study]])[1]*dim(count_dfs[[study]])[2])
  print(paste0(study," : Sparsity = ", sparsity))
}

remove_zero_rows_cols <- function(mat) {
  keep_rows <- rowSums(mat != 0) > 0
  keep_cols <- colSums(mat != 0) > 0
  result <- mat[keep_rows, keep_cols, drop = FALSE]
  return(result)
}

for(study in studies){
  
  matrix = count_dfs[[study]]
  matrix_removed = remove_zero_rows_cols(matrix)
  
  sparsity = sum(matrix_removed == 0)/(dim(matrix_removed)[1]*dim(matrix_removed)[2])
  print(paste0(study," : Sparsity = ", sparsity))
  
}

#Hence there are no completely zero columns

#Removing samples that have less than 5 species 
remove_sparse_columns <- function(mat, min_nonzero = 5) {
  # Count non-zero entries in each column
  nonzero_counts <- colSums(mat != 0)
  
  # Keep only columns with at least min_nonzero non-zero entries
  keep_cols <- nonzero_counts >= min_nonzero
  
  # Subset the matrix, preserving matrix structure even if one column remains
  result <- mat[, keep_cols, drop = FALSE]
  
  return(result)
}

for(study in studies){
  
  matrix = count_dfs[[study]]
  matrix_filt = remove_sparse_columns(matrix,5)
  
  sparsity = sum(matrix_filt == 0)/(dim(matrix_filt)[1]*dim(matrix_filt)[2])
  print(paste0(study," : Sparsity = ", sparsity))
  
}

#OK so sparsity changes when I filter out the samples with less than a particular species abundance. I will see if I can reverse the order
study = studies[3]

#Applying custom filter first 
matrix_skin_desparsed = remove_sparse_columns(count_dfs_unfiltered[[study]],5)
meta_desparsed = meta_dfs_unfiltered[[study]][colnames(matrix_skin_desparsed),]
res <- simbaR:::check.original.data(matrix_skin_desparsed, meta_desparsed, sim.type="cross-section", sim.method="resampling")
feat.checked <- res$feat
meta.checked <- res$meta

#Filtering
filt.params <- simbaR:::check.filtering.parameters(filt.params)
count_df_1 <- simbaR:::filter.data(feat = feat.checked, meta = meta.checked, filt.params = filt.params)

sparsity_1 = sum(count_df_1 == 0)/(dim(count_df_1)[1]*dim(count_df_1)[2])
print(paste0(study," : Sparsity = ", sparsity_1))

#Applying custom filter second
count_df = count_dfs[[study]]
count_df_2 = remove_sparse_columns(matrix,5)

sparsity_2 = sum(count_df_2 == 0)/(dim(count_df_2)[1]*dim(count_df_2)[2])
print(paste0(study," : Sparsity = ", sparsity_2))

#comparing matrices
```

```{r,fig.height=6,fig.width=6}
#Summary stats of datasets – to determine what aspects of the datasets are causing the difference in effects – plotting actual data - boxplots of library size, counts per species, number of species – ggbeeswarm to get actual points on top of boxplot

#Library Size Boxplot

#Collecting library sizes
library_sizes = list()

for(study in studies){
  library_sizes[[study]] = meta_dfs[[study]][,c("Library_Size","Individual_ID")]
}

library_sizes_melt <- melt(library_sizes)
names(library_sizes_melt) = c("individual_ID","variable","library_size","study")

library_sizes_melt = library_sizes_melt %>% mutate(study = case_when(
  (study == "OhJ_2014_filtered") ~ "OhJ_2014",
  TRUE ~ study)
)

library_sizes_melt = library_sizes_melt %>% mutate(study = case_when(
  (study == "OhJ_2014") ~ "Skin",
  TRUE ~ study)) %>% mutate(study = case_when(
  (study == "Zeevi_2014") ~ "Gut",
  TRUE ~ study)) %>% mutate(study = case_when(
  (study == "Brito_2016") ~ "Oral",
  TRUE ~ study)
)

library_sizes_melt[["Niche"]] = library_sizes_melt[["study"]]

ggplot(library_sizes_melt, aes(x=study, y=library_size,col=Niche)) +
  geom_boxplot(outliers=FALSE,show.legend=FALSE) +
  geom_jitter(width =0.2,alpha=0.5,size=0.7) +  # Jittered points
  xlab("Niche") +
  ylab("Library size of each sample") +
  ggtitle("Sample library size comparison between niches") +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 13))
ggsave("NicheSummary_plots/library_size_comparison.png")
```

```{r}
summarise_count_matrices <- function(matrix_list, digits = 2) {
  # Name the matrices if the list is unnamed
  if (is.null(names(matrix_list))) {
    names(matrix_list) <- paste0("matrix_", seq_along(matrix_list))
  }

  summary_list <- lapply(matrix_list, function(m) {
    m <- as.matrix(m)  # also accepts data frames / sparse-to-dense inputs

    n_species <- nrow(m)
    n_samples <- ncol(m)

    data.frame(
      n_samples             = n_samples,
      mean_nonzero_species  = mean(colSums(m != 0)),   # avg number of non-zero species per sample
      mean_library_size     = mean(colSums(m)),        # avg total count per sample
      mean_count_per_entry  = mean(m),                 # avg count of a species in a sample
      sparsity              = mean(m == 0)             # fraction of entries equal to zero
    )
  })

  result <- do.call(rbind, summary_list)
  result <- cbind(matrix = names(matrix_list), result, row.names = NULL)

  # Round the numeric summary statistics (n_samples stays an integer count)
  stat_cols <- setdiff(names(result), c("matrix", "n_samples"))
  result[stat_cols] <- lapply(result[stat_cols], round, digits = digits)

  # Print a formatted copy so trailing zeros are kept (e.g. 10.00, not 10)
  display <- result
  display[stat_cols] <- lapply(result[stat_cols], format, nsmall = digits)
  print(display, row.names = FALSE)

  invisible(result)
}

summarise_count_matrices(count_dfs,2)
```
